lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Hedged the bank's interest-rate risk on its fixed-rate bond holdings by buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
- Cut the monthly close from 8 working days to 5 by automating 30 reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Mapping 600 general-ledger accounts to a new chart of accounts, rebuilding the allocation rules and testing them against two prior closes, cut manual journal entries from 350 to 90 a month.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Trained 5 plant controllers on the new budgeting template and wrote its user guide.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Showed the share value fell from USD 50 to USD 40, a 25% drop, when the discount rate rose by 1 point.
- Raised the model's forecast accuracy by 12% across 10 years, from 70% to 82%, by adding rate-case timing.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Wrote onboarding notes on the fund's models for new analysts.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It does not establish qualifications and creates privacy and age-discrimination concerns.

items.says: Remove nationality unless an application specifically requires it.
items.because: Nationality is generally irrelevant to evaluating financial-analysis experience.

items.says: State work authorization separately if it matters for the role.
items.because: Nationality alone does not establish work authorization.

items.says: Use a direct, working LinkedIn URL rather than a placeholder.
items.because: The listed address may be anonymized or may not lead to the professional profile.

items.says: Standardize date formatting and dash style across the résumé.
items.because: Date ranges should use one month format and one dash style.

items.says: Check whether the degree uses the university’s official format.
items.because: The degree designation should be consistent.

items.says: Consider adding strong, relevant GPA, honors, scholarships, or coursework.
items.because: They could add useful evidence without merely filling space.

items.says: Keep education concise and visually secondary to recent employment.
items.because: The résumé now shows substantial experience.

items.says: Consider identifying the credit portfolio or coverage area.
items.because: It would help employers understand the role.

items.says: Buying more same-duration fixed-rate bonds does not generally hedge the stated interest-rate risk.
items.because: It generally adds exposure to the same risk rather than offsetting it.

items.says: Clarify the exposure being managed and the actual hedging method.
items.because: The bullet may instead concern liability duration, an offsetting position, or another exposure.

items.says: Add a measurable result if there was one.
items.because: Without one, the bullet may be too weak to retain in its current form.

items.says: Remove “my findings.”
items.because: First-person possessive wording is not conventional résumé style.

items.says: Define the population and period behind the approval-rate change.
items.because: It is unclear whether the figures describe a pilot, a portfolio-wide change, or another comparison.

items.says: Define the time window for “early defaults.”
items.because: The default claim needs a relevant measurement period.

items.says: Be prepared to substantiate the claim that defaults did not rise.
items.because: Interviewers may ask for support for that assertion.

items.says: Change “Writes” to past tense.
items.because: The role ended in 2022, and the present tense clashes with the other experience bullets.

items.says: Clarify whether the checklist was created, implemented, or maintained.
items.because: The current wording does not establish the scope of the work.

items.says: Specify what the figures 7 and 1 count.
items.because: It is unclear whether they refer to missed tests, borrowers, or incidents.

items.says: Include the portfolio scale if the checklist was adopted broadly.
items.because: That would strengthen the impact.

items.says: Clarify “spreading” for applications beyond banking.
items.because: General recruiters may not know the term.

items.says: Say what workflow the three-hour time saving was measured across.
items.because: It could describe a team, portfolio, or typical analyst workflow.

items.says: Mention use by other analysts or fewer review errors if supported.
items.because: That would provide useful context for the template.

items.says: Give the most recent role the strongest bullet ordering and appropriate space.
items.because: It is presumably the most relevant role.

items.says: Verify the June 2025 end date and use a current-employment date if applicable.
items.because: An ongoing job should not show June 2025 as its end date.

items.says: Define what “USD 600M” measures.
items.because: Company size is hard to interpret without knowing whether it is revenue, assets, or something else.

items.says: Qualify the claim that the forecast let treasury repay debt early.
items.because: That may overstate causality unless treasury explicitly relied on the forecast.

items.says: Give the period over which forecast error stayed under 4%.
items.because: A measurement period makes the result more credible.

items.says: Add verified interest savings if the early repayment produced them.
items.because: They would make the repayment’s impact clearer.

items.says: Name relevant tools or systems used for the automation.
items.because: They may matter to the target role.

items.says: Clarify what the count of 30 covers.
items.because: Reconciliations and intercompany eliminations may be separate categories of work.

items.says: Add a verified reporting or manual-effort benefit of the faster close.
items.because: It would show the operational consequence more fully.

items.says: Explain the business benefit of the shared capital-plan template.
items.because: The stated result is less compelling than the other bullets.

items.says: Verify that one discount rate for all projects was approved policy.
items.because: Projects can require different risk-adjusted rates, so one rate could sound financially unsophisticated.

items.says: Quantify any effect on approvals or capital deployment.
items.because: That would show the template’s decision impact.

items.says: Change the opening to a clear past-tense verb and subject.
items.because: The bullet begins as a fragment and obscures who did the work.

items.says: Prioritize or separate the several activities in the long bullet.
items.because: Mapping, rule rebuilding, testing, and journal-entry reduction compete for attention.

items.says: Clarify whether this work alone caused the reduction in journal entries.
items.because: Other process changes may have contributed.

items.says: Explain “two prior closes” if the validation matters to the role.
items.because: The current description does not make the testing process clear.

items.says: Include a relevant accounting system or automation tool in Skills if appropriate.
items.because: This is a systems-and-process accomplishment.

items.says: Correct the FCFE/WACC valuation mismatch.
items.because: FCFE is generally discounted at the cost of equity, while WACC is generally paired with FCFF.

items.says: Add a result, recommendation, valuation range, or decision impact.
items.because: The bullet currently states only the valuation activity.

items.says: Add the analysis’s scale or purpose if confidentiality permits.
items.because: The context would make the M&A work clearer.

items.says: Specify an outcome of training the controllers if available.
items.because: Adoption, training time, submission quality, or error reduction would show impact.

items.says: Say whether the guide became a standard reference across sites.
items.because: That would strengthen its scope.

items.says: Do not let projects overshadow professional accomplishments.
items.because: The résumé already shows several years of experience.

items.says: Check whether “Present” still reflects the project’s status.
items.because: A completed project should have a completion date.

items.says: Add company or sector context if it is not confidential.
items.because: That could improve the project’s credibility.

items.says: Clarify the project’s scope and whether it was personal, academic, or investment-related.
items.because: It ran alongside full-time employment.

items.says: Give a date or valuation point for the market-price comparison.
items.because: Market prices change continuously.

items.says: Identify the two values compared in “within 6%.”
items.because: The reader cannot tell precisely how the difference was calculated.

items.says: Do not present proximity to market price as proof of accuracy.
items.because: A close valuation is not necessarily independently validated.

items.says: Change the claimed 25% drop to 20%.
items.because: A fall from USD 50 to USD 40 is a 20% decline.

items.says: Specify that “1 point” means one percentage point.
items.because: It could otherwise be read as a 1% relative increase.

items.says: Identify whether this was a sensitivity, scenario, or base-case change.
items.because: The type of analysis is unclear.

items.says: Say whether USD 50 was the model value or market price.
items.because: The distinction matters.

items.says: Label the improvement as percentage points or a relative percentage.
items.because: A rise from 70% to 82% is 12 percentage points but about 17% relative.

items.says: Explain how forecast accuracy was measured.
items.because: The claim is difficult to evaluate without a metric.

items.says: Clarify what “across 10 years” refers to.
items.because: It could mean a forecast horizon, historical testing, or ten observations.

items.says: Establish whether the model was validated against realized results.
items.because: Adjusting a model to fit historical data is not the same as validation.

items.says: Consider reducing or removing the older Student Investment Fund entry.
items.because: It should earn space by adding investment-analysis evidence not already shown in professional experience.

items.says: Make the individual contribution within the team clearer.
items.because: “Team of 6” does not itself establish meaningful ownership.

items.says: Clarify whether the fund actually had an FP&A team or this bullet belongs elsewhere.
items.because: The reference is potentially inconsistent with a Student Investment Fund.

items.says: Replace the vague “Supported” description with specific work and impact, or remove it.
items.because: It does not show what was personally done or what changed.

items.says: Identify the benchmark and reporting period.
items.because: That could better demonstrate the analysis behind the report.

items.says: Quantify the report’s frequency or reach if possible.
items.because: The number of meetings, holdings, or analysts affected would strengthen the impact.

items.says: Verify the claim that the committee used the report at every meeting.
items.because: Its use should not be merely inferred.

items.says: Specify how many models the notes covered and whether they became a standard resource.
items.because: The bullet lacks scale and outcome.

items.says: Prioritize analytical and investment outcomes ahead of this onboarding bullet.
items.because: It is a secondary accomplishment.

items.says: Expand the thin Skills section.
items.because: It provides little detail for someone with several years of financial-analysis experience.

items.says: Specify demonstrable Excel capabilities.
items.because: “Excel” alone is too broad to show the features used.

items.says: Add other tools actually used, including relevant Stonebridge platforms.
items.because: Employers may want to know the systems behind the work described.

items.says: Replace or supplement the broad, repetitive methods with more specific ones.
items.because: The experience shows narrower capabilities that could be named.

items.says: Make capitalization and punctuation consistent.
items.because: The skills should follow one presentation style.

items.says: Ensure each listed method is supported by the experience bullets.
items.because: Skills should reflect demonstrated work rather than introduce unsupported capabilities.

items.says: Prevent manual line-break hyphenation in the document.
items.because: Words such as “fixed-rate” should wrap naturally rather than be split by added hyphens.
